sources.entry: Get It - Native macOS video/audio downloader. Think of it as a youtube downloader that works on many sites.

summary.one_liner: Get It is a native macOS GUI for downloading audio and video from many websites, built as a front end around the youtube-dl command-line tool.
summary.what_it_does: The app wraps youtube-dl in an easy-to-use graphical interface, so users can download videos or audio from sites such as YouTube, BBC and Instagram without using the terminal. Its default settings download the audio from a video, convert it to MP3, and save it to the Downloads folder. Settings are saved automatically, and users can restore the defaults. A settings screen includes an 'Install/update software' button that installs or updates the required command-line dependencies through Homebrew. The README also describes uninstall steps for the developer tools and Homebrew-managed components. Troubleshooting covers common errors such as 'Something went wrong', which is usually fixed by updating youtube-dl, and it explains how to collect logs from /tmp/getit_logs for bug reports.
use_cases: download YouTube videos to a Mac
extract MP3 audio from online videos
save videos from many websites without the terminal
batch-convert web video to audio files
how_to_run: Download the app from the link in the README, unzip it, and open it.
Open the app's settings and click 'Install/update software' to install the dependencies.
Alternatively, install the dependencies manually in Terminal using the commands in the README (Xcode command line tools, Homebrew, Python, Python 3, PyCrypt, youtube-dl, libav, ffmpeg).
notable: Simple GUI wrapper around youtube-dl with a built-in dependency installer
Default mode extracts audio and converts it to MP3
Settings are saved dynamically and can be reset to defaults
Logs at /tmp/getit_logs help with bug reports
caveats: macOS only, and requires Homebrew to install its dependencies
Relies on youtube-dl, so site support and fixes depend on updating that binary
Uses Python 2.7 pip for PyCrypt, which is an older toolchain
